title: Choose a clear chart
summary: A chart should fit the question. Bars compare category counts. A line can show ordered measurements over time. Labels must name the values and units.
introduction: A chart should fit the question. Bars compare category counts. A line can show ordered measurements over time. Labels must name the values and units. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.title: Choose a clear chart

blocks.text: The bar lengths show the counts. Starting bars at zero helps keep the visual size comparison fair.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a title that includes the week being measured.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A chart with missing units or a misleading scale can suggest the wrong story.
For more detail later, use this [Data Science further reading](https://www.openintro.org/book/ims/).
